hunt at all
b - He is not forced to pay if he has no blood, so he skips the payment
and go hunting

a - He cannot hunt so he stay ready

instead of a "melee weapon" ??

can already play -ser- inferior)...
what's happening now ? Does he gain the superior -SER- ???

Thanks

Messages.Author: John
Messages.Body:
"Akaisuisei" <sam-ga...@libero.it> wrote in message
news:z8e79.71396$lu5.2...@twister1.libero.it...

I'll answer what I know and leave the rest to more knowledgable,

> 4- My Setite plays Sanguine Instruction (Serpentis) upon Ian Forrestal
(that
> can already play -ser- inferior)...
> what's happening now ? Does he gain the superior -SER- ???

From card text of Sanguine Instruction:
"Choose a Discipline this vampire has at superior. Put this card on a ready
vampire of the SAME CLAN as this acting vampire."

So first off a setite cannot play Sanguine instruction on Ian or any other
clan other than another Setite. But if Ian had clan impersonnated into a
Setite you could then do this.
The result is that Ian has lesser serpentis. To gain SER the Setite would
have to do it again. Ian's card text refers only to master cards.

ut=gplain

B: actually, superior StH just make the acting vampire to "move" blood to
the
vamp who has "slaughtered" him/her, it has nothing to do with "paying"
something to attempt the action, so the "slaughtered" vamp just "skip" the
*move blood* thing.

>
> 2- I play inferior Reality on one of my vamps to avoid being rushed, but
my
> minion reach 0 blood... the Reality forbid him to do anithing other than
> burn Reality... what's happening now ?
> a - He cannot hunt so he stay ready

>

A: he should hunt, he cannot, so he's stuck and can't take no action.

> 3- Do anybody know if the new Talbot Chainsaw will still be a "weapon"
> instead of a "melee weapon" ??

"Will" ? Don't know in the upcoming CE, anyway the talbot has been always
a (unique) "weapon", not a melee weapon.

>
> 4- My Setite plays Sanguine Instruction (Serpentis) upon Ian Forrestal
(that
> can already play -ser- inferior)...
> what's happening now ? Does he gain the superior -SER- ???

No, only Master:discipline cards grants Ian the superior version of the
discipline.
Ian doesn't "have" the disciplines he can play by his ability, so a sanguine
instruction
grants him the normal level of a discipline.

> "John" <verg...@hotmail.com> wrote in message

> > ut=gplain

> anyone know how to keep a link together when posting a link from Google?
> (somebody must) It
> appears as one line on the message I send but arrives in two parts.

You're using Outlook Express.
Somewhere in the options/preferences area should be a setting for wrapping
lines of your composed messages to some value, probably 72. Change this
value to something larger, like 200, and then press [RETURN] yourself.

I use Netscape 4.76. With the preferences so adjusted, your link looks
like this when I post it:

http://groups.google.com/groups?selm=3C68F785.F3DB038C%40white-wolf.com&output=gplain

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <3D5D8C6B...@white-wolf.com>, LSJ <vtesrep@white-

wolf.com> writes:
>You're using Outlook Express.
>Somewhere in the options/preferences area should be a setting for wrapping
>lines of your composed messages to some value, probably 72. Change this
>value to something larger, like 200, and then press [RETURN] yourself.

For Outlook Express, there is also the option of using QuoteFix. It's
not something I use myself - not using OE - and it offers a lot more
features too. However, amongst its features list it mentions:

# Reformat: re-assemble unquoted broken URLs (where detectable)

This may be of use to people, I'm not entirely sure. It fixes a lot of
other things too.

http://home.in.tum.de/~jain/software/quotefix.php is the link I've
always been given. It appears to redirect now, but still works.

A number of news-readers are also mildly intelligent with split-up URLs
and will allow them to be reassembled quickly. (Mine does, for
instance.)

--
James Coupe
